topic_candidates.brief: Break down the viral claim that Claude helped produce a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. Then show what actually makes this story unusual—the proof was released as millions of lines of Lean code that a proof checker can replay, rather than as a short human-readable argument. ([leanprover-community.github.io](https://leanprover-community.github.io/blog/posts/riemann-hypothesis/?utm_source=openai))

topic_candidates.query: Claude Riemann hypothesis proof Lean Alpoge Mathlib independent verification explained
topic_candidates.brief: Tell the same viral story from a different angle: not “AI magically solved math,” but “how can we check an AI-generated proof?” Walk viewers through the difference between a language model proposing a chain of reasoning and Lean mechanically checking every accepted step. topic_candidates.evidence_summary: The Lean community says the released library contains a formal proof targeting Mathlib’s own Riemann Hypothesis statement, with independent tools comparing the theorem statements and checking the proof modules. The source supports a verification explainer, not an unsupported claim that all consequences are immediately understood. topic_candidates.science_angle: The engineering principle is proof-carrying computation: the result is bundled with machine-checkable evidence. Lean’s kernel checks whether each deduction follows from the formal definitions and permitted axioms, which is fundamentally different from asking an AI model whether its answer looks convincing.
